summary: BUG: Mobile – Asset Expand Icon Misaligned, Making Mileage Field Difficult to Access
reported_issue: On the mobile Work Order view, the asset section expand/collapse icon is misaligned and positioned too close to the asset switch icon, creating a touch-target conflict that makes it hard to expand the asset section and access the Mileage field.
expected_after_fix: Mileage should be easily accessible for technicians; the expand arrow should be repositioned so it does not conflict with the asset switch icon.
steps_i_followed: Emulated an iPhone (390x844, isMobile+touch, iPhone UA) via Chromium and opened a Work Order detail (S9-15740).
Inspected the top asset/summary card and enumerated its icons and their coordinates.
Toggled the 'Show Details' control to expand the full Customer and Asset cards.
Located the asset card's switch icon and the expand/collapse control and confirmed Mileage is present in the expanded asset card.
actual_now: The mobile asset area has been reworked. The compact WO card shows a single edit-pencil icon (top-right, ~25x25px) with no crowded expand-arrow/switch-icon pair. Expansion is now driven by a distinct, clearly-labeled 'Show Details / Hide Details' toggle (text + chevron) at the top of the section. In the expanded view each card (Customer, Asset) has a single swap/switch icon (⇄) in its own top-right corner, well separated from the 'Show/Hide Details' collapse control. Mileage is present and reachable in the expanded asset card. No misalignment or touch-target conflict between an expand arrow and the asset switch icon was observed.
notes: Tested via Chromium mobile-viewport emulation (responsive/mobile-web is testable per harness rules). The specific crowded/misaligned expand-vs-switch icon layout described in the ticket no longer exists; the expand/collapse is a separate labeled control and Mileage is accessible. Confidence medium because the exact original account's card ('1/off Kustoms, LLC') could not be reproduced, but the general current mobile asset-card layout does not exhibit the reported conflict.
